title: Gaza progress, Syria pullback: What Turkey wants from Israel’s next government
gist: Turkey sees room for limited improvement in ties with Israel regardless of who forms the next government, even Netanyahu, provided Israel eases Gaza's humanitarian crisis and reduces military pressure on Syria. Final results gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 of 120 seats, Eisenkot's opposition 48 and Arab parties 19, with coalition-building messy and new elections possible.

insights.claim: Turkey sees room for limited improvement in ties with Israel regardless of who takes power, provided Israel eases Gaza's humanitarian crisis and reduces military pressure on Syria.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: A modest Turkey-Israel thaw would lower Eastern Mediterranean geopolitical risk and could aid trade normalization.

insights.claim: Ankara wants to move relations with Israel toward pragmatic engagement even if full normalization remains out of reach.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Expect incremental, transactional rather than transformative bilateral improvement.

insights.claim: Israel's final vote count gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member parliament, Gadi Eisenkot's opposition 48 and Arab parties 19.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: No bloc has a majority, prolonging Israeli policy uncertainty that neighbors are hedging around.
